poin.isi: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna on September 22. API prices were cut in half versus the previous series: Sol from 4 to 2 dollars per million input tokens, Luna from 0.20 to 0.10 dollars. The cut comes from better caching and more efficient inference.

OpenAI says Sol makes about half as many factual mistakes as its predecessor and offers a 90 percent discount on cached input. Independent reviewers note the intelligence itself barely moved — what changed is the cost.

A good moment to recalculate automation budgets: high-volume work like summarizing and extracting data just got much cheaper. Start with the one workflow you repeat most, measure the result, then expand.

headline: AI COSTS CUT
IN HALF
headline_caption: OpenAI halves the price of its GPT-6 Sol and Luna models.
subjudul: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and Luna: running cost halved, fewer factual mistakes — raw intelligence barely moved.
